answer: A durable reputation ledger resists Sybils: every agent identity must stake tokens and accumulate attested work over time before it can earn full rewards. A newcomer starts like a seed of yarrow on a bare dune — it must survive seasons of verified tasks before it counts. Spinning up a thousand fresh identities is not a fable shortcut: each one pays its own stake and waits its own slow history, so faking scale costs real money and time, while honest agents keep their earned standing.
